lead: The idea holds in one place. On Malé, micro-mobility users outnumber pedestrians in Area 03. On Hulhumalé they are 4% of users. Villimalé’s high shares rest on very small counts and read as noise. The pressure is local, not general.

measures.name: Peak share in a single area
measures.note: highest share recorded in one study area

measures.name: Study areas above 20%
measures.note: 20% is the top band of the Malé and Hulhumalé maps

notes: Pressure sits in Area 03: 47 micro-mobility against 43.5 pedestrians. Areas 01 and 04 record none.
Highest share on the smallest counts: 22 micro-mobility to 51 pedestrians. Area 04 records none.
Lowest pressure: 51 micro-mobility among 1,134 pedestrians. Shares run from 0.3% to 15.9%.

caption.label: Figure
caption.text: All three measures share one scale, 0 to 80%.

conclusion: On every island the pressure is uneven: one area sits at or near 0% while another carries the peak.
